# Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**RE:** Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09
**Member:** Emerson Alvarez
**Member ID:** W977514824
**Reference number:** POC-4E415360FE-32022
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 ([link](https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf))

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement surgery (CPT 27130), which was denied on 2026-08-09 for "incomplete documentation." I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I believe the records already submitted address what the plan's own policy requires.

## Why I believe the documentation is complete

Cigna's policy states:

> "hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

The specific condition categories quoted to me in this policy excerpt name femoral head/neck fracture and avascular necrosis. My diagnosis, as shown on my weight-bearing AP pelvis X-ray from 2026-06-02, is joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes — findings consistent with degenerative joint disease, not a fracture or avascular necrosis. I want to be transparent that the specific osteoarthritis criteria language was not included in the materials I have to quote from, so I am not able to quote that section back to Cigna directly. I am asking Cigna to review my case against whatever section of its own policy governs degenerative joint disease of the hip, since that is my documented condition.

What I can show, based on my own records, is that I have provided the kind of clinical information the policy generally asks for before approving hip replacement:

**Imaging.** My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph from 2026-06-02 showed joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.

**Function-limiting symptoms.** I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. I currently walk with a cane and can only go about one block before the pain stops me. I cannot put on my shoes without help.

**Failed non-surgical management.** The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

I completed 16 weeks (20 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, from 2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also tried NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-15 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This is well beyond the three-month period the policy describes, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

**Exam findings.** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion, and I have no active infection or untreated substance use that would affect surgical candidacy.

The policy also states, regarding when the standard non-surgical management period may not apply:

> "Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

I raise this only to note that, in my case, I did complete conservative management well past three months, so this exception is not something I need to rely on — but I mention it in case Cigna's reviewer is evaluating whether the record shows enough non-surgical treatment. My physical therapy records, medication trial, and injection date should establish that this requirement was met.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Cigna to review the physical therapy discharge note, the imaging report from 2026-06-02, the medication and injection records, and my surgeon's clinical notes together, and to reconsider the denial in light of this documentation. If any specific piece of information is still considered missing, I would appreciate a clear description of exactly what is needed so my surgeon's office and I can provide it.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am submitting it by logging in at my.cigna.com to find the appropriate appeal form, and/or by calling the number on my member ID card (1-800-244-6224). I understand the mailing address for a written appeal is the one printed on my denial letter, and I am using that address if mailing this letter.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal. I would appreciate a written response confirming what materials, if any, are still needed.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Emerson Alvarez
Member ID: W977514824

Femoral Head/Neck Fracture • Imaging shows a fracture of the femoral head or femoral neck • Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option Avascular Necrosis (AVN) • Imaging shows avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head • Symptoms include BOTH of the following:

◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration ▪ Criteria exception:
Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate.

◦ loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration ◦ Criteria exception:
The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate.
